title: Cost Volatility Is Making Early Contractor Involvement Essential for Winnipeg Architects

blocks.x: A volatile cost environment

Early contractor involvement matters more when costs move quickly. Metals and mechanical and electrical components led a rise in Winnipeg construction costs of 4% or more in 2025, according to [Altus Group's 2026 Cost Guide insights](https://www.altusgroup.com/insights/caution-in-2026-optimistic-for-2027-cost-guide-insights/). Altus ties the metal increases to US tariffs and trade uncertainty at the national level.
Labour costs are rising with inflation too. In Winnipeg, Altus says availability is holding steady with demand expected to grow; across Canada, it calls shortages the most persistent constraint.

Since Altus published in April 2026, conditions have tightened. The Bank of Canada [raised its policy rate to 2.50%](https://www.bankofcanada.ca/2026/10/fad-press-release-2026-10-28/) on October 28, 2026, with oil prices persistently high and new US tariffs expected to slow growth.

[Statistics Canada](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/daily-quotidien/261019/dq261019a-eng.htm) put September 2026 inflation at 3.1%, and the Bank's [Monetary Policy Report](https://www.bankofcanada.ca/publications/mpr/mpr-2026-10-28/tariff-assumptions/) says trade talks with the United States broke down in late August.
For architects, that means the cost assumptions behind a design can change between schematic design and tender. Projects that come in over budget can lead to redesign, delays and frustrated clients.
Where renovation projects go wrong
Renovation work is especially prone to surprises because the existing building is never fully known until demolition starts. Common issues include:
**Hidden conditions:** rotted framing, damaged masonry, outdated materials behind walls.
**Hazardous materials** such as [asbestos in older buildings](/blog/asbestos-testing-before-renovating-manitoba).
**Unexpected structure** that limits planned openings or layouts.
**Long-lead items,** such as windows and storefronts, that do not arrive in time.
**Material substitutions** forced by availability or price.
Each surprise costs time and money, and puts pressure on the design team.
Our view: early involvement de-risks design
Bringing a contractor in during design, rather than at tender, gives architects real-world input when it is still cheap to change course. A good construction partner can:
**Provide cost feedback** on design options as they develop.
**Investigate existing conditions** through selective demolition or exploratory openings, once suspect materials have been tested.
**Advise on sequencing,** especially in occupied buildings.
**Flag long-lead and tariff-exposed items** so they can be ordered early or substituted.
**Suggest alternatives** that achieve the design intent at lower cost or risk.

Not every contractor offers all of this, so ask each one what they do during design and whether it is paid work. The value is in a construction partner who understands both design intent and how buildings are actually put together.

blocks.x: Engagement models
Architects and clients can involve contractors early in several ways:
**Pre-construction services agreements**, where the contractor is paid for estimating, constructability reviews and investigations.
**Construction management**, with the contractor engaged through design and construction.
**A site walk against the drawings**, where the contractor checks the drawings against the building and raises conflicts before work starts.
Each model has different implications for procurement and fees, and the right choice depends on the client and project.
Making the case to clients

Some clients resist paying for pre-construction services, seeing them as an extra cost. Architects can make the case by pointing to the cost of redesign after a failed tender, the risk of hidden conditions in renovation work and the value of early ordering for long-lead items.
In a volatile market, paying for early contractor input can help protect the overall budget.
What to watch

Watch the Bank of Canada's December 9, 2026 decision and trade developments with the United States. Both can affect project financing and material costs in 2027. Projects in design now should build in flexibility for either outcome.
An example from existing-building work

This is a made-up illustration, not a real job. Consider a masonry building being renovated for a new use. The design calls for a wider opening in an interior masonry wall. Exploratory openings during design suggest that the wall is load-bearing and in poor condition.

Discovering this during design allows the architect to adjust the layout and a structural engineer to assess the wall and plan repairs before tender. Discovering it during construction would mean change orders, delays and difficult conversations with the client. Early contractor involvement turns surprises into design inputs.
The bottom line

Cost volatility makes early contractor involvement more valuable. Winnipeg architects who bring construction partners into the design process can test costs, uncover existing conditions and help protect their clients' budgets.
